transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because I… I can’t really stop worrying. It’s a lot of things at once—my marriage, work, bills, stuff around the house I keep not finishing. And I keep feeling like I’m failing as a husband and a dad.
Have you been avoiding any activities or situations because of your worries?
I don’t know… I guess I haven’t really thought of it that way. I’m not sure if I’m avoiding things, exactly.
Can you think of any situations or activities that you used to enjoy but haven't been doing lately?
I’m not sure. I mean… I don’t really keep track of what I used to do for fun. Lately it’s mostly just work and home stuff. Nothing specific is coming to mind.
Have you been avoiding any social situations because of your worries?
I don’t think so… not specifically social stuff. I mean, I haven’t really noticed myself avoiding people because of worry.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?
I don’t know… not really sad, I guess. More just… I haven’t paid much attention to it.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?

Yeah… I guess I do. I feel kind of wound tight most of the day, like my shoulders are locked up and I’m bracing for something. I’ll catch myself pacing between meetings, or tapping pieces at chess club because sitting still just feels… hard.
Have you been feeling more tired than usual lately?
I’m not sure. I mean… maybe a bit, but I haven’t really been tracking it.
Have you had any thoughts of not wanting to be alive?
I… don’t really know. I mean, I haven’t been thinking about it like that, not that I’ve noticed.
Have you had any significant changes in your appetite lately?
Not really sure. I haven’t noticed a big change… I’m eating, I guess, about the same.
Do you have any recurring thoughts or mental images that you can't get out of your head?

Yeah… sort of. It’s not like images so much. More like worries that keep chaining together. I’ll try to focus on my code, or even just get through a workout, and then one thing turns into another… like a bad review becoming me losing my job, and then my family being worse off because of me. It’s hard to shut off.
Do you feel like these worries are unreasonable or excessive?

Yeah… I mean, part of me knows it’s probably too much. I came in because I can’t really stop worrying about everything at once—my marriage, work, bills, stuff around the house I keep dropping… and then it turns into me thinking I’m just failing as a husband and father.
Do you feel like these worries are intrusive, meaning they come into your mind even when you're trying to think about something else?

Yeah. It kind of cuts in even when I’m trying not to think about it. I’ll tell myself to just focus on the code, or just get through a workout, and then one worry grabs onto another… and suddenly I’m way ahead, thinking a bad review means I lose my job and my family ends up worse off because of me.
How long have you been experiencing this excessive worry?
About nine months, I guess. It got worse when the cloud migration at work ramped up… and around then the arguments at home started happening a lot more.
Has something very stressful or traumatic happened to you in the past, especially around the time your worries started or worsened?
Nothing traumatic, no. It’s more… it’s been about nine months, since the cloud migration got intense and the arguments at home started being a regular thing.
Have you been doing things to try to avoid thinking about your worries?
I don’t know… maybe sometimes. I’ll try to keep busy or distract myself, but I’m not sure I’d call it avoiding. It doesn’t really work for long anyway.
Is there one particular thing, like the cloud migration at work or the arguments at home, that you think is causing most of your worry?
Not really one thing. It’s more like… all of it at once. Work, my marriage, bills, stuff around the house I keep dropping. I just keep thinking I’m slipping, like I’m failing as a husband and father.
Do you think your worries started or got significantly worse after the cloud migration at work and the arguments at home began?
Yeah… I think so. It’s been about nine months, around when the migration really picked up and the arguments at home started happening more regularly. Since then it’s just been… more constant.
Have you experienced any significant stressor or change in your life that you think triggered the start of your excessive worrying?
Yeah… I think it started around then. About nine months ago, when the cloud migration got heavier and things at home started turning into regular arguments. Since then it’s been harder to shut off.
Have your worries been present for more days than not over the past six months?
Yeah… definitely more days than not. It’s been about nine months now, since work got heavier and the arguments at home became more regular.
Have your worries been making it hard for you to function in your daily life?

Yeah… it has. Work especially. My manager’s started writing down missed architectural details, which… isn’t great. And at home I’m not finishing things, I’m distracted, and then the arguments just get worse.
